question.problem:
On a certain afternoon, the total number of people $N(t)$ visiting the city's zoo is given by the function

$$
N(t)=25+3{\int }_{0}^{t}(8-2x)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time (in hours) since noon.  

At what time is the number of people in the zoo at a maximum, and how many people are at the zoo at that time?
question.worked_solution:
To find when the number of people at the zoo is at maximum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(25+3{\int }_{0}^{t}(8-2x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(25)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{\int }_{0}^{t}(8-2x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(8-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(8-2t)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=0$:

$$
3(8-2t)=0\,⟹\,t=4
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=4.$ To find out how many people are in the zoo when $t=4,$ we figure out $N(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(4) & =25+3{\int }_{0}^{4}(8-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =25+3{[8x-{x}^{2}]|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =25+3[(8\cdot 4-{4}^{2})-(0)] \\  & =25+3\cdot 16 \\  & =73\end{aligned}
$$

Since $25<73$, we conclude that the maximum number of people at the zoo is $73$, and this will happen after $4$ hours.
